title: Tasks with more than one input
idea: Some tasks start with several things. Name all of them, not just one.

exercises.prompt: Task: 'Add two prices to get a total.' How many inputs does it have?
exercises.explanation: Two prices go in, one total comes out. Count every value you start with.

exercises.prompt: Task: 'Average three test scores.' What are the inputs?
exercises.explanation: All three scores are inputs. Missing one would give the wrong average.

exercises.prompt: If a task says 'two meals and three drinks', the counts (two and three) are part of the input.
exercises.explanation: Yes — every number in the task is an input. Don't drop the counts; they matter.

exercises.prompt: Task: 'Buy 2 pens and 1 notebook; show the total cost.' Which of these are inputs? (Choose all.)
exercises.explanation: Counts and prices are all inputs. The total cost is the output, not an input.

exercises.prompt: Task: 'Buy 2 pens and 1 notebook; show the total cost.' What is the output?
exercises.explanation: The one thing that comes out is the total cost.

exercises.prompt: It is fine to ignore one of the inputs if the task has several.
exercises.explanation: Never drop an input. Every value in the task is there for a reason — leaving one out breaks the result.

exercises.prompt: Match each task to how many inputs it has.
exercises.explanation: Count the values you start with. That count is how many inputs the task has.

exercises.prompt: Task: 'Split a bill of 60 between 4 people.' What are the inputs?
options: The bill (60) and the number of people (4)
exercises.explanation: Both 60 and 4 go in. The amount each person pays is the output.

exercises.prompt: For 'Split a bill of 60 between 4 people', which are TRUE? (Choose all.)
options: The number of people is an input
The amount per person is the output
exercises.explanation: Two inputs (bill and people count), one output (amount per person). The last option is false.

exercises.prompt: Writing down every input first helps make sure none gets forgotten later.
exercises.explanation: Listing all inputs up front is a safe habit — it stops you dropping a value when you solve the task.
